title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 196 (Right of person as to acts done for him without his authority)

content.overview: Where acts are done by one person on behalf of another, but without his knowledge or authority, he may elect to ratify or to disown such acts. If he ratify them, the same effects will follow as if they had been performed by his authority.
content.glance: Unauthorized acts done on one’s behalf may be ratified or disowned; ratification has the same effect as prior authority.
content.study: Where acts are done by one person on behalf of another, but without his knowledge or authority, he may elect to ratify or to disown such acts. If he ratify them, the same effects will follow as if they had been performed by his authority. Read with ss. 197–200 on form, knowledge, whole transaction, and third-person protection.

sections.heading: Acts without knowledge or authority
sections.body: Acts done on behalf of another without his knowledge or authority.

sections.heading: Election to ratify or disown
sections.body: The person may elect to ratify or to disown such acts.

sections.heading: Effect of ratification
sections.body: If ratified, same effects as if performed by his authority.

provisions.title: Right of person as to acts done for him without his authority

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 196 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Identify unauthorized acts done on behalf of the person; state the election to ratify or disown; if ratified, apply as if authorized, subject to ss. 197–200.
